items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: My brother was a professional violinist. He was about — let me see, Dave would have been — oh he was about 13 or 14 years older than I am.

ctx.x: When you were a youth, was there music in your house a lot?

Quite a bit, yeah, actually. My brother was a professional violinist. He was about — let me see, Dave would have been — oh he was about 13 or 14 years older than I am. He was born in Russia actually. I was born in Boston in 1920. And my sister also played the violin. And I also took the violin. There is about six or seven years between us. There’s quite a spread in the family there. And I played the violin and viola, and studied with a very fine teacher at Boston, Carl Barladen was his name. He was with the…

dinner hour or something like that. And then I went on and I played in clubs. They had after hour clubs. And an after hour club was one that opened about eleven or twelve o’clock at night when the legitimate clubs so to speak were closing, and you could get a drink in there. And they had trios and quartets that consisted of either violin, the cello — not the cello — violin and guitar and bass, occasionally a piano might have been in there. And people used to come in there, and they were quite orderly places, and…
